items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: the maturity and the subtlety of a Lockjaw Davis or a Jimmy Forrest was a little bit lost on me.

ctx.x: But you’re not talking about chord changes, you’re talking about like emotional—

No I’m talking about structure changes, emotional. The vividness and the drama again is really what I think I was caught up with originally. And the sort of maturity and the subtlety of a Lockjaw Davis or a Jimmy Forrest was a little bit lost on me. Because I didn’t have any connection to the source material that they were taking off from. I mean I heard that is, American standards are corny; not necessarily corny. I liked them when Fred Astaire sang them, but I didn’t feel like this is a vehicle for spilling out…
You’ve mentioned the vocal connection. People, instrumentalists, using vocal — loss for words here — vocal inflections.

items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: when I would go to hear music by some of the aging, really the swing masters: Jimmy Forrest, Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis, guys like this.

ctx.x: I mean I think that there’s this mythology that you have to know everything about jazz or jazz is some sort of heady music that is not accessible readily. I’ve never understood that exactly. I mean it’s so dramatic. I can understand it, when I would go to hear music by some of the aging, really the swing masters: Jimmy Forrest, Eddie “Lockjaw” Davis, guys like this. Now they were a little bit past their prime I supposed by the time I was hearing them in the late sixties. And they did not represent what I…

making melodies, they’re just making a lot of notes. And the interaction there, although I think the jazz people understand very well the kind of interaction that’s going on, I think to the listener who’s not exposed in a deep way, it sounds pro forma. And you do not hear the interaction between the drummer and the saxophonist and the pianist who’s comping for the soloist. You don’t hear it as something that’s being created afresh. Now again, maybe it’s because these guys were a little bit past their prime, they…
